text:
jess: Heads-up — multiple tenants on eu-west dedicated are hitting sudden 429s + p95 token latency spikes. Customer: Zipcart. Looks like the autoscaler is doing a repeat up/down dance (2 <-> 4) every ~6m, causing throttles.

mike: saw the alert, grabbing logs. tenant=zipcart-prod, pool=eu-west-dedicated-a

anya: can you paste the scale events? infra-bot should have them.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] scale_up target=4 actual=2 reason="queue_depth>200" ts=2026-11-02T12:04:23Z
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scale_down target=2 actual=4 reason="cpu<10%" ts=2026-11-02T12:09:29Z
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scale_up target=4 actual=2 reason="queue_depth>220" ts=2026-11-02T12:15:35Z
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scale_down target=2 actual=4 reason="cpu<12%" ts=2026-11-02T12:21:41Z

mike: quick prometheus check I ran: 
```
max_over_time(scaler_target_replicas{pool=\"eu-west-dedicated-a\"}[10m])
```
returns the same oscillation, spike windows match customer 429s.

lucas: pattern looks like: short-lived queue spike -> immediate scale_up -> prefix/KV cache warms -> load falls -> quick scale_down. With scale_down cooldown at 120s we still hit the cycle.

jess: customer complains 429s mainly during the scale_down transition. Need mitigation ASAP.

anya: Proposed quick fixes: increase scale_down_cooldown to 600s and set min_replicas=3 for that pool/tenant. That should absorb transient bursts. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

mike: +1. Also change trigger metric to a smoothed queue metric so we don't react to 30s spikes. e.g. `avg_over_time(queue_depth[3m]) > 80` instead of instant queue_depth.

jess: can we roll a canary? snippet:
```
infractl update-pool --pool eu-west-dedicated-a \\
  --policy scale_down_cooldown=600s \\
  --policy min_replicas=3 --target=canary
```

triage-bot: Incident #INC-2026-512 created: "eu-west dedicated autoscale instability causing 429s". Assigned to mike.

mike: starting canary now. I'll tail router logs + token latency dashboards.

lucas: FYI I pulled tenant metrics for alpha-analytics (same pool) — they had repeated KV invalidations and cache misses right before the queue spikes. Could be a noisy neighbor causing the short surges. If so, we should consider tenant isolation or stricter tenant-specific min_replicas limits.

jess: good catch. For immediate relief, tweak cooldown + smoothing. If we still see bursts after 1h, escalate to dedicated eng for tenant isolation.

mike: quick commands/logs I ran:
```
# check active reqs per replica
sum(rate(requests_total{pool=\"eu-west-dedicated-a\"}[30s])) by (replica)
# 1-min avg queue
avg_over_time(queue_depth{tenant=\"zipcart-prod\"}[1m])
```
results: p95 token latency dropped from ~1.8s -> 0.35s after canary deploy, 429s reduced to 0 within two scale cycles.

anya: I'll open a short RFC to change default autoscaler behavior for dedicated pools: longer scale_down cooldown, smoothed queue metric, tenant-level min_replicas option, and an autoscale blacklist for known noisy tenants.

jess: :thumbsup: Thanks team. Monitoring window set to 45m. If stable, we'll promote canary to prod for that pool and notify the customer.

mike: update at +20m: metrics stable, no 429s, p95 holding ~0.4s. Leaving monitor for remaining window.

lucas: filing a support note to contact alpha-analytics if we continue to see KV churn — might be a runaway batch job.

jess: closing loop when monitor ends. Great work.
